concept.reason: Primary figures directly cover skeletal and filament gates; no extra concept image needed.

scope: Complete small long-armed tyrannosauroid with filamented body outline, three-fingered hands, full trunk, legs and balancing tail.

scientific_limits.en: V14243 skull and skeletal anatomy and1.6m estimate anchor reconstruction, not a measured living adult. Filament evidence is from V11579, provisionally referred to D.paradoxus in2004 but possibly a second closely related Dilong species. Do not claim same specimen or certain same species. Filaments preserved by distal tail and posterior mandible; coverage elsewhere, density, colours and soft tissue inferred. Fig2 shows fragmentary V11579 preserved bones inside restored silhouette; not a complete fossil.
scientific_limits.zh: V14243头骨和骨骼及1.6米估值为主锚，非活体成年实测。丝状体被来自V11579，2004暂归D.paradoxus但原文明言可能另一近缘帝龙种，不冒称同一标本或确定同种。实际体被在尾远端及后下颌附近，其余覆盖、密度、颜色和软组织为外推。图2仅显示V11579部分已知骨骼，其完整轮廓为复原。

taxon: Dilong; skeleton anchored to D.paradoxus IVPP V14243, integument to referred IVPP V11579

scale.basis: Xu etal2004 estimate for largest known specimen IVPP V14243, not complete living measurement.

diagnostic_targets: Light small biped with proportionally long neck and trunk, slender balancing tail.
Long forearms with three discrete clawed digits each, not tiny two-fingered derived tyrannosaur hands; palms inward.
Short filament tufts break body and tail silhouette; branching filament reference, not broad aerodynamic wing feathers or a bird tail fan.
Relatively low lightly built skull with modest Y-shaped nasal/lacrimal ridge, not deep Tyrannosaurus skull or tall Guanlong crest.
Complete body retains forelimb negative space and readable joint transitions.
specimen_basis: Actually viewed Xu etal2004 Fig1 V14243 skull and humerus photos/drawings, Fig2 V11579 partial skeletal diagram and Fig3 V11579 actual filament photographs.
acceptance_checks: Original319 gate retained: small long-armed tyrannosauroid and filamented outline together, not name/size/pose-only distinction.
Compare standard side view forelimbs and body silhouette with primary Fig1/2; three fingers and long arms distinguish derived short-armed tyrannosaurs.
Compare filament tufts to Fig3, avoid smooth naked silhouette or broad flight-feather wings.
Front/top confirm inward hands and restrained cranial ridge, not Guanlong crest.
Explicitly disclose V11579 provisional species assignment and inferred coverage; four standard views only, no original extra named comparison-render requirement.
